about: Ghar.tv component library. Generated by scripts/build-components.mjs from _dev/reference/components/*.html. Do not edit by hand.

howToUse.paste: Copy "snippet" into the page. If status is "inline", also copy "style" into the page <style>. Load every file in "css" and "js".
howToUse.include: Never paste this markup. Put the PARTIAL marker pair in the page, add the body classes in "snippet", then run npm run build:partials.
howToUse.call: Load every file in "js", then call the function shown in "js_snippet".

rules: Guidelines (why and when) live at /design-system. No em dashes. Brand red #ee324b only on logo, primary CTA and interactive states. White is the page ground.

.sec-title for the section's display heading; --md for sub-section heads, --sub for the related and more-from modules under an article, --sm for a compact tracked-caps title
.sec-lead for the one or two sentences that set a section up

Negative letter-spacing or italics on Gazpacho
Shrinking a title to fit long copy. Give it width (.sec-title--wide) rather than smaller type

components.name: Button
components.summary: The general-purpose .btn chassis for page actions that are not the section CTA: load more, a strip's view-all, a contribute panel's two actions. One base class for geometry, one modifier for the colour role.
use: .btn.btn-primary for a quiet, outlined page action: Load more, All stories in a tag strip
.btn.btn-accent for the one dark, filled action of a panel, such as Pitch a conversation or Download media kit
.btn.btn-ghost when the button sits on a dark ground and needs a translucent white outline
avoid: The section header CTA. That is .btn-text, one per section
A CTA inside a card. Cards use the card link (.btn-link) or link as a whole
Red fills. Red is reserved for page-level brand actions such as Post Property
Pairing .btn-accent with .btn-primary side by side: on hover the outline fills with ink and both buttons turn dark. Use the paired CTA instead
Redefining .btn or .btn-ghost in a page <style> block. Some B2B pages do, and the local rule silently overrides the shared one

api.name: .btn-quiet

api.name: svg
api.desc: Optional trailing icon. .btn does not size it, so give the svg width and height attributes or a page rule.

components.name: Card link
components.summary: The text plus arrow cue that sits inside a card: no border, no fill, 13px ink. On hover the gap widens and the arrow slides; the colour never changes.
use: The inner cue of a whole-card link, as a <span> inside the card's <a> (Explore finance)
A standalone read link in a quiet context, with .btn-link--underline, when nothing else on the block says link
The last line of a card body, with .btn-link--gap-top so it clears the description
avoid: The section's main CTA. That is .btn-text in the section head
A pill or bordered button inside a card: it competes with the section CTA
A red hover. Text links stay ink and motion is the only hover cue
An <a> nested inside a card that is already an <a>. Use a <span class="btn-link"> there

api.name: .btn-link
api.desc: Inline-flex text + arrow, 13px Inter 600 ink, no wrap. Hover widens the gap 6px to 9px and slides the svg 2px.

api.name: .btn-link--underline
api.desc: 1px underline at 4px offset, thickens to 2px on hover. For a block with no other link chrome.

api.name: .btn-link--gap-top

api.name: svg
api.desc: Trailing arrow, sized 12px by the class. Keep aria-hidden.

.arrow-link for a single See more affordance where red is earned

.arrow-link more than once in a view: red stays near 5% of the page
Either one as a section CTA (.btn-text) or a card cue (.btn-link)
A red hover on any other text link

components.name: Paired CTA
components.summary: The canonical treatment whenever two buttons sit side by side: the main action dark, the secondary a quiet white that only warms on hover. The hierarchy survives the hover state.
use: Any two actions on one line: Cancel and Confirm in a modal, Back and Continue in a form step
As the colour source for inline page pairs with their own geometry (the person profile hero pair takes its colours from here)
avoid: A transparent secondary that inverts to ink on hover. Two dark buttons side by side lose the hierarchy
Two primaries. One view, one committed action
Putting the primary on the left. The secondary sits left so the primary keeps the rightmost position
Changing the colours when the geometry has to change. Geometry may be local, colour may not

api.name: .jm-btn--secondary

components.name: 3-column editorial grid
components.summary: A supporting left column, a prominent centre column and a supporting right column. On phones the columns stack; between 576px and 1079px the centre spans the top with the sides paired below; from 1080px it is three columns with hairline dividers around the centre.
use: An editorial roundup or hero where one story leads and two columns of lighter items flank it (the /design hero and Inspiration roundup)
.grid-3col-editorial--center-first when the centre column must come first on a phone even though it sits in the middle of the DOM

Turning the side columns into a carousel below 1080px. The tablet layout is the shared rule; forking it to a rail is what this replaced
Reordering columns in page CSS. Use the modifier

components.name: Panel bleed
components.summary: A contained, rounded content panel that becomes a full-width band below 1024px, so its content lands on the same gutter as every other section instead of being indented twice on a phone.
use: A tinted or bordered panel inside a section that holds a whole block: a process grid, an FAQ, a stat table
Any panel where the rounded box is presentation rather than meaning
avoid: A small card, a callout, or one item among several. Those should read as discrete objects, not stretch to the viewport
A whole <section> that should run edge to edge. That is section.section--bleed
Styling the panel's border-radius or padding outside a min-width: 1024px query. A plain page rule outranks this single class and the bleed half-applies
Escalating the utility with !important to win that fight

api.name: .panel-bleed

api.name: page rule
api.desc: The page owns background, border-block and padding-block at every width, and states its contained look (border, radius, padding-inline) only inside @media (min-width: 1024px).

.section-head__link when a bordered .btn-text would be too heavy for the head

Putting the See all in the foot row under a carousel. The foot row is for arrows and dots

Switching between views of one subject. That is tabs

A red separator or a red current page. The trail is muted and ink only

components.name: Load more
components.summary: A single button under a directory grid that reveals the next batch in place. The shared gharGridReveal helper counts whole rows off the live column count, so no batch ever leaves a ragged part-row, and it hides the button when nothing is left.
use: Directory and archive grids where the reader is grazing: /brands, /people, a pillar tag page
Any grid that already holds all its items in the DOM and should show them a few rows at a time
avoid: Infinite scroll. It makes the footer unreachable and hides how much is left
Counting a fixed number of cards. The same 12 is 4 rows at 3-up and 12 rows at 1-up; batch in rows
A spinner and a Loading label when the items are already on the page. The button reveals, it does not fetch
A dead button that stays visible after the last batch. The sentinel takes .is-done and hides
Numbered pages here. Use pagination only when a reader needs to return to a known position

api.name: .br-loadmore

api.name: .is-done

api.name: .is-hidden

Server-rendered paged results, with each page as a real URL
avoid: Editorial browsing where the reader is grazing. Use load more
The carousel dot row. That is .dc-paginator
Removing Prev on page one. Keep it with aria-disabled="true" so the row does not shift under the cursor
A count without the total. Page 1 of 12 alone does not say whether paging on is worth it

components.name: Segmented control

An .active class. aria-selected (tabs) or aria-checked (choice) is the only state, and the CSS keys off it
A per-page click handler. No init call is needed; a second listener is how the two meanings drift apart

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: Grey placeholder blocks with a soft sweep, shaped like the content about to arrive. The sweep stops under reduced motion, and the class hides any text already inside the element.
use: The gap between a request and its answer, where the final layout is already known: a card grid, a byline
On an element that already holds its real text while that text loads: .skeleton makes the text transparent
avoid: A shape that does not match what lands. That is worse than a spinner; the correction reads as a glitch
A block of identical bars. Vary the widths so it reads as text

use: The Spotlight placement on /brands and /people, above the directory grid
Rotating several paid or nominated tenants through one slot, one per day
avoid: Painting the panel in the tenant's hex. Identity comes from their logo, their photography and one accent keyline; the surface stays white
A stock photo when a brand has no photography. The block is identity-led and the media is optional
Tenant-coloured CTAs. The CTA is ink-filled so its label passes contrast for any tenant
@media breakpoints inside the block. .if-block is a container; every breakpoint is @container
A Sponsored badge or section-level sponsorship wording without a disclosure decision

components.name: Checkbox, radio and switch
components.summary: The small choice controls of the form system. The native input stays in the DOM and is visually replaced, so keyboard, submission and assistive tech work with no extra code. The whole label is the hit area.
use: Checkbox: a short list of words where several can be on, committed on submit
Radio: one answer out of a few (up to five)
Switch: a setting that takes effect the moment it flips, like a notification preference
avoid: A switch inside a form that commits on submit. That is a checkbox
Radios past five options. Use a select
A set the reader should scan and compare (amenities, property type). Use chips or tiles
Removing the native input or hiding it with display:none, which breaks keyboard and form submission

api.name: .jm-check
api.desc: Checkbox row on a <label>. Holds the native input, .jm-check__box and the text.

api.name: .jm-check__box
api.desc: The painted box. Carries the tick path M20 6L9 17l-5-5.

api.name: .jm-radio
api.desc: Radio row. Same shape as the checkbox, with .jm-radio__dot as the painted mark.

api.name: .jm-switch
api.desc: Switch row, min-height 44px. Native checkbox plus .jm-switch__track and .jm-switch__text.

api.name: .jm-switch__text small
api.desc: Optional second line under the switch label explaining what flipping it does.

api.name: disabled
api.desc: On the input. The row mutes and the cursor changes; the option stays visible.

components.name: Either/or choice
components.summary: A two or three answer question (buy or rent, residential, commercial or land) drawn as one segmented switch. Radio semantics on the .seg paint, with a single thumb that slides and resizes to the chosen answer and stacks when the labels cannot fit one row.
use: A question with two or three known, short, mutually exclusive answers
A step in a flow where the answer is recorded, not a view that swaps a panel
avoid: Switching views or panels. That is the tab version of .seg with role=tablist
More than five answers (use a select) or answers that need explaining (use tiles)
.seg--ink beside a filled button. One filled object per view: pair the light thumb with a .btn-text step action
Wiring the setter to an inline onclick. Listen for the bubbling change event, or the arrow keys stop updating state

api.name: .seg.seg--choice
api.desc: The group. Carries role=radiogroup and an aria-label.

api.name: .seg__btn
api.desc: Each answer: a button with role=radio. aria-checked is the only state; unchosen ones take tabindex=-1.

api.name: .seg__ico
api.desc: Optional two or three stroke line icon before the label, on currentColor.

api.name: .seg--ink
api.desc: Dark thumb. Only on a surface with nothing else filled.

api.name: change
api.desc: Native change fired on the chosen button and bubbling, from pointer and keyboard alike.

api.name: gharSegThumb(group, animate)
api.desc: Re-fits the thumb after you set aria-checked from code, or after a hidden group becomes visible. Pass false to land without the slide.

api.name: gharSegFit(group)
api.desc: Re-decides row versus stacked layout for a group whose container width changed without a resize.

components.notes: In production on the search modal's Mode and Type steps, which carry extra mob-* hook classes and inline stopPropagation for that modal. Drop those in any other context.

components.name: Enhanced select
components.summary: A plain select.jm-field that main.min.js upgrades on load into a portal-styled trigger and option panel, with keyboard, type-ahead and flip-up. The native select stays underneath and keeps owning name, value, required and form.reset().
use: Any list under about a dozen options inside a portal form
A select added after load (a modal body injected later): call initJmSelects on its container
avoid: Hand-writing .jm-select markup. It is generated; write the plain select and let the script wrap it
A per-page custom dropdown (the old .brs-sort). This does it once for the form system
A list nobody can scan, such as countries or every city. That needs a searchable panel
Reading value from the visible trigger. Read the native select, which fires change as usual

api.name: select.jm-field
api.desc: The markup you write. First option is the prompt: value="" and, for required fields, disabled.

api.name: aria-label
api.desc: Required. Copied to the generated trigger so it is announced.

api.name: initJmSelects(root)
api.desc: Enhances every select.jm-field inside root (default document). Runs on load; safe to call again, already enhanced selects are skipped.

api.name: data-jm-select
api.desc: Set by the script on each enhanced select as its idempotency guard. Never author it.

api.name: .jm-select
api.desc: Generated wrapper holding .jm-select__native (hidden), .jm-select__trigger and .jm-select__panel of .jm-select__opt rows. Flips up with .jm-select--up near the viewport bottom.

api.name: change
api.desc: Fired on the native select when an option is picked, so existing listeners keep working.

components.name: Field label, required mark and help
components.summary: A persistent label above a .jm-field, an optional red asterisk for a field that blocks submit, and a muted help line tied to the control. For long multi-section flows where a placeholder would vanish as the reader types.
use: Long flows such as Post Property or the SuperPro application, where the reader loses the thread halfway down
A field whose expected answer needs one line of explanation (carpet area versus built-up)
avoid: Short modals (sign in, contact, brief). They stay placeholder-driven; do not add labels just because you can
Colouring the label red. Only the asterisk carries the functional red
Help text that repeats the label in other words. If it adds nothing, delete it
Help text without aria-describedby, which strands it for screen readers

api.name: .jm-label
api.desc: Label above the control, 13px 600 ink. Always a real <label for>.

api.name: .jm-req
api.desc: Red asterisk inside the label. aria-hidden, since the input carries required.

api.name: .jm-help
api.desc: Muted help line under the control. Negative top margin tucks it against the field.

api.name: aria-describedby
api.desc: On the control, pointing at the help line's id so it is announced with the field.

components.snippet: The usable floor area inside your walls, in square feet. Not built-up or super built-up. Optional for resale. Required for any under-construction listing.

components.name: Field states and errors
components.summary: Error, valid and disabled states for .jm-field, the per-field error line, and the form-level error above submit. gharFieldError moves the red border, the message and aria-invalid together so none is left behind.
use: Telling the reader one field is wrong: a named cause and the shape of a valid answer, shown after they leave the field
A form-level summary above the submit button when the form as a whole cannot be sent (.brf-error)
A confirmed value that genuinely helps, such as a verified phone number (.is-valid)
avoid: Toggling .is-error or the message by hand. Always go through gharFieldError so border, text and aria-invalid move together
Swapping the two: .jm-field-err is per field, .brf-error is the form-level summary
Apologetic or vague copy. Say what happened and how to fix it
Green on every correct field. Most correct fields need no colour; sage is only for a confirmation that helps
A toast for one field's error

api.name: gharFieldError(field, message)
api.desc: Sets the error on a control: adds .is-error, sets aria-invalid, writes the message into the element its aria-describedby names and unhides it. Pass null to clear.

api.name: .is-error
api.desc: Red border on .jm-field. Set by gharFieldError, not by hand.

api.name: .is-valid
api.desc: Sage border on .jm-field, for a confirmation that helps.

api.name: .jm-field-err
api.desc: Per-field message line with its icon. Starts hidden; its id goes in the control's aria-describedby.

api.name: .brf-error
api.desc: Form-level error strip above submit, role=alert, hidden until needed.

api.name: disabled
api.desc: Warm grey fill and muted text. Disabled, never hidden.

components.notes: Debt: gharBriefSubmit in main.js does not use gharFieldError yet. It paints its own .is-invalid class (styled only under #brBriefModal) and writes every message into .brf-error. New forms use gharFieldError.

components.name: File upload drop zone
components.summary: A drop zone over a real file input: click to open the picker or drag files onto it. Chosen files list underneath with their size and a remove button, wired by main.min.js through data-file-list.
use: Photos on Post Property, a portfolio on the SuperPro application, any form that takes files
Stating the real limits (type, size) in the hint before anyone uploads
avoid: A bare <input type="file">, which cannot be styled and reads as unfinished next to .jm-field
Changing the fill colour on hover or drag. The dash darkens, and .is-drag closes it to solid ink; the fill stays warm white
Treating the client list as validation. Size and type must be checked again on the server

api.name: .jm-file
api.desc: The zone, on a <label> wrapping the native input, so a click anywhere opens the picker.

api.name: data-file-list
api.desc: On the input: the id of the .jm-file-list to render chosen files into. Self-wiring, no init call.

api.name: .jm-file__icon / __label / __hint
api.desc: Upload icon, the action, and the limits line.

api.name: .jm-file-list
api.desc: Empty <ul> that main.min.js fills with name, size and a .jm-file-remove button. Collapses while empty.

api.name: .is-drag
api.desc: Set on .jm-file while files are dragged over it.

components.name: Form field
components.summary: The one control class of the portal form system. .jm-field paints text, email, select and textarea identically, .jm-phone pairs a mobile input with the +91 prefix, and .brf-row puts two controls on one line.
use: Every text, email, phone, select or textarea control on the portal, in a modal or on a page
Short forms, which stay placeholder-driven: each control says what it is inside itself
Two short related answers side by side (type and city, budget and timeline) with .brf-row
avoid: A separate select or textarea class. .jm-field covers all of them, and adding one is how a fork starts
A third prefix (.form-*, .brf-input). Extend .jm-* instead
Brand tints on a control. Form UI stays warm and monochrome, even on a tenant page
Placeholder-only controls on a long multi-section form: those need a persistent label

api.name: .jm-field
api.desc: The control. Put it on input, select and textarea alike: 1.5px rule border, 14px radius, ink border on focus.

api.name: .jm-phone
api.desc: Mobile number wrapper. The inner input takes no class; the wrapper draws the box.

api.name: .jm-phone-prefix
api.desc: Static flag and +91 before the input. The sign-in modal swaps this for the searchable country-code button.

api.name: .brf-row
api.desc: Two controls on one line as a 1fr 1fr grid. Drops to one column below 560px. The only layout class a form needs.

api.name: aria-label
api.desc: Required on every select, whose first disabled option doubles as its visible label.

components.snippet: +91
components.notes: Every select.jm-field is upgraded to the custom panel by main.min.js on load. See the Enhanced select component for that behaviour.

components.name: Long-form structure
components.summary: Sections for a long form: .jm-fieldset groups with an eyebrow legend, a line of intro and a hairline between them, a live character counter under a capped textarea, and the .jm-actions row with the form buttons.
use: A form that genuinely has sections, such as Post Property or the SuperPro application
A textarea with a maxlength the reader should see coming (data-counter)
A secondary plus primary action pair at the end of a form or dialog
avoid: Fieldsets in a six-field modal. Short forms need none of this
Putting the primary on the left. Secondary sits left, the most committed action keeps the rightmost position
A red legend. The legend is an eyebrow: 10px, uppercase, faint
.jm-btn--danger anywhere but an irreversible action in a confirm dialog

api.name: .jm-fieldset
api.desc: A <fieldset> group. Adjacent fieldsets get a hairline and top padding between them.

api.name: .jm-legend
api.desc:
The group's , styled as an eyebrow. A following

becomes its muted intro.

api.name: data-counter
api.desc: On a textarea or input: the id of its .jm-counter. Paints used / maxlength on input and on load. Self-wiring.

api.name: .jm-counter
api.desc: Right-aligned tabular count under the control. Gets .is-over at the limit.

api.name: .jm-actions
api.desc: One row of buttons, 12px apart.

api.name: .jm-btn
api.desc: The form button: full width on its own, shared across flex space in .jm-actions.

api.name: .jm-btn--primary
api.desc: The commit. One per view.

api.name: .jm-btn--secondary
api.desc: White with a field rule; the non-committing action.

api.name: .jm-btn--danger
api.desc: Red fill, only for the irreversible action in a confirm dialog.

components.name: Project brief form

use: A page whose whole job is taking a brief, where the form sits in the page instead of a dialog
Changing a brief field: edit partials/brief-form.html once and every surface follows
avoid: Pasting the fields. They are regenerated between the PARTIAL markers
Carrying it inline AND including the brief modal on the same page. The ids are fixed and would collide
Adding labels. The brief is a short form and stays placeholder-driven; selects carry aria-label
Renaming fields without the backend. POSTed names are source, name, phone, email, projectType, city, budget, timeline, message

api.name: #brBriefError

api.name: data-brief-open
api.desc: On a page with this form and no modal, a trigger scrolls the form into view and focuses the name field.

components.name: Selection chips and tiles
components.summary: Large selection controls where the option itself is the target. .jm-chip is a pill for many short options, .jm-tile a block for a few that need explaining. Both are native checkboxes or radios underneath, styled off :has().
use: A set the reader scans and compares: amenities, configuration, the whole filter sheet (chips)
Two to a handful of options that each need a sentence, such as construction stage or furnishing (tiles)
Options carrying a third-party logo, via the white logo plate
avoid: A solid ink selected fill. The 2px ink outline carries the state; a black logo on an ink fill disappears
Brand rose, blush, petal or mist, or an ink alpha, as a selected fill. Foundation tones only
Hiding an unavailable option. Disable it so the reader knows it exists
A count of zero shown as a live chip. Disable it
Setting an .is-selected class from JS. State follows the input through :has()
Two or three fixed, mutually exclusive answers. That is the either/or control

api.name: .jm-chip-row
api.desc: Wrapping flex row of chips. Wraps rather than scrolls so nothing hides off-screen.

api.name: .jm-chip
api.desc: A pill on a <label> holding a checkbox (many on) or radio (exactly one). Clears 48px.

api.name: .jm-chip--sm
api.desc: Dense chip for filter sheets. Still clears 40px.

api.name: .jm-chip__icon
api.desc: Optional line icon on currentColor.

api.name: .jm-chip__count
api.desc: Muted result count after the label.

api.name: .jm-chip__logo
api.desc: White plate holding a partner mark so the selection fill never lands behind it.

api.name: .jm-chip__logo--dark
api.desc: Dark plate for white-on-transparent marks. Same on .jm-tile__logo--dark.

api.name: .jm-tile-grid
api.desc: auto-fit grid with a 260px floor, so two columns become one on a phone without a breakpoint.

api.name: .jm-tile
api.desc: A block option with .jm-tile__icon (or __logo) and .jm-tile__body holding __title and __desc.

api.name: .jm-tile--stack
api.desc: Icon above text, for picture-led tiles. Pair with .jm-tile__check.

api.name: .jm-tile__check
api.desc: Opt-in tick badge, only where a border alone reads as decoration.

components.name: Submit success panel
components.summary: What replaces a form in place once it is sent: a sage tick, a Gazpacho title and a line that says what happens next. The reader who just sent a brief gets a destination, not a message that vanishes.
use: After submitting a brief, an enquiry or an application, swapping out the form inside the same modal or page block
Pairing the confirmation with one onward secondary action
avoid: A toast for a submitted brief. Toasts are for actions that need no follow-up
An alert() box. The brief and contact modals still use one as a stub; this panel is the intended replacement
Copy that says nothing (Thanks for your submission). Say what happens next and by when, only if that is true
A primary filled button in the panel. The commit already happened

api.name: .jm-success
api.desc: Centred panel. Show it and hide the form (hidden attribute) in the same step.

api.name: .jm-success__mark
api.desc: 56px sage-tinted circle holding the tick.

api.name: .jm-success__title
api.desc: Gazpacho 22px headline.

api.name: .jm-success__body
api.desc: Muted line: what happens next.

components.name: Brand contact modal
components.summary: Contact a brand: an editorial two-line heading with the brand's name, then name, mobile, optional email and a short note. The brand name travels in a hidden field. Used on the brand directory, brand search, brand profiles and people pages.
use: An enquiry addressed to one named brand, from a brand card, a brand profile or a person's affiliated brand
avoid: Pasting the markup. It is regenerated from partials/br-contact-modal.html
A general project enquiry with no brand. That is the brief modal
Copying another page's inline brContactOpen script into a new page without checking the trigger it listens for; the copies have drifted

api.name: #brContactBrand
api.desc: The subject line of the two-line .jm-heading (Contact / Brand).

components.name: Confirm dialog
components.summary: A small modal that asks before an action that cannot be undone. A red-tinted mark, a question, the consequence in plain words, and two buttons: the safe choice left, the destructive verb right in the one red fill the form system allows.
use: Deleting or withdrawing something that cannot come back: a listing, an account, a sent application
avoid: Anything reversible. Do it immediately and offer Undo in a toast instead
OK or Yes on the destructive button. It carries the action's own verb (Delete listing)
Describing the mechanism. Name the consequence the reader has to weigh
The destructive button on the left, or a red fill anywhere else in the form system

api.name: .jm-confirm
api.desc: Centred body content, inside .jm-body of a .jm-size-sm modal.

api.name: .jm-confirm__mark
api.desc: 48px circle in rgba(238,50,75,.10) holding a red line icon.

api.name: .jm-confirm__body
api.desc: The consequence, muted, 14px.

api.name: .jm-btn--danger
api.desc: Red fill for the destructive button. Pair with .jm-btn--secondary on its left in .jm-actions.

api.name: .jm-modal--no-fullscreen
api.desc: Keeps the dialog a centred card on phones rather than a full-screen sheet.

api.name: role="alertdialog"

components.name: Image lightbox
components.summary: Full-size image viewing with Fancybox v6.1 from the CDN. Links carrying the same data-fancybox group open as one gallery with prev and next, captions and thumbnails; /gt-fancybox.js layers the portal's tap behaviour on top: a backdrop tap steps back instead of closing, and Work slides cycle caption, cover and fit.
use: A set of images a visitor wants to see full size, such as certificates: wrap each thumbnail in a link to the large image with data-fancybox="group" and data-caption
Binding a group once with Fancybox.bind and passing options through gtFancybox.mergeDefaults
avoid: PDFs. Leave data-fancybox off so the link opens the file in a new tab
Adding Toolbar or Panzoom overrides to fix mobile. Earlier custom configs killed Fancybox's built-in drag, pinch and double-tap
Styling .fancybox__container or .fancybox__backdrop without checking gt-fancybox.js, whose interceptors key off those nodes
A light lightbox. Image viewing is one of the few surfaces reserved for a dark overlay

api.name: data-fancybox="group"
api.desc: On a link whose href is the large image. Links sharing a group open as one gallery.

api.name: data-caption
api.desc: Caption text shown with the image.

api.name: Fancybox.bind(selector, options)
api.desc: Fancybox's own binder, called once per group after fancybox.umd.js has loaded.

api.name: gtFancybox.mergeDefaults(options)
api.desc: Pass-through for shared options; installs the portal tap interceptors (idempotent; the file also installs them itself on DOMContentLoaded) and returns the options unchanged today.

api.name: fancybox.sidebar.css / fancybox.sidebar.umd.js
api.desc: The sidebar plugin, loaded after the core files on profiles whose Work lightbox shows image and caption side by side.

components.notes: Nine brand profiles load Fancybox, but only scarlet-splendour, studiofov and teearch load /gt-fancybox.js; the other six bind groups without the portal interceptors, so backdrop taps close instead of stepping back there. Each profile also carries its own inline bind block (certs, gallery, work) rather than a shared binder. The certificate thumbnail (.bpr-cert, .bpr-cert__media, .bpr-cert__name) is styled only by page-inline CSS in each profile and template; brand-profile.min.css has just its list, img and hover rules, so the snippet here stays class-free until the tile moves to dist.

components.name: Modal shell
components.summary: The one chassis every portal modal rides: .jm-overlay plus .jm-modal at a size token, an optional title row with the close button, and .jm-body as the single scroll container. Toggle .jm-open on both to show it. Below 744px it becomes a full-screen sheet that slides up.
use: A task that genuinely cannot continue underneath: signing in, sending a brief, contacting a brand, confirming something irreversible
Any new modal. Start from these classes instead of an ID block of its own
avoid: Sticky or fixed chrome inside the modal. The body scrolls everything together, header and close included
position:fixed on body to lock scroll, or visualViewport height syncing. The lock is the body.jm-scroll-locked class, nothing else
Leaving role="dialog" off. main.min.js finds modals by it to add the scroll lock and back-button close
A dark modal by default on a dark page. Modals stay light unless the content is inherently dark (.jm-modal--dark)
var(--ink) as a primary button fill on a dark tenant, where --ink is remapped to cream. Use the red primary
Opening without a way back: overlay click, the close button and Escape must all close it

api.name: .jm-overlay
api.desc: Fixed backdrop, z-index 310, 50% black with a 2px blur and touch-action:none so iOS cannot rubber-band the page behind.

api.name: .jm-modal
api.desc: Fixed centred panel, z-index 315, 20px radius, max-height min(92vh, 820px). Needs role="dialog", aria-modal and a label.

api.name: .jm-size-sm | -md | -lg | -xl
api.desc: 420, 480, 540, 660px (capped at 92vw). sm a confirm, md sign in or a short form, lg a standard form, xl only for real horizontal need.

api.name: .jm-open
api.desc: On both overlay and modal: fades and scales in. Removing it closes.

api.name: .jm-hdr
api.desc: Title row: title left, close right, hairline below. Not sticky.

api.name: .jm-hdr-title
api.desc: Inter 14px 600 utility title for functional modals (Sign In, a confirm).

api.name: .jm-heading
api.desc: Gazpacho editorial title for content modals. A child <span> gives the two-line preamble plus subject (Contact / Brand).

api.name: .jm-subtext
api.desc: Muted dek under the heading.

api.name: .jm-close
api.desc: 36px round close. Inside .jm-hdr, or as the first child of .jm-modal for a title-less modal (floats right, flex-end).

api.name: .jm-body
api.desc: Owns the padding and is the only scroll container, with overscroll-behavior:contain. A form inside becomes a 14px gap column.

api.name: .jm-modal--no-fullscreen
api.desc: Keeps a tiny confirm as a centred card on phones instead of the full-screen sheet.

api.name: .jm-modal--dark / .jm-overlay--dark
api.desc: Opt-in dark surface (#0F0F0F, cream title) and a heavier 70% backdrop, for inherently dark content.

api.name: body.jm-scroll-locked
api.desc: Added by main.min.js (and dist/bpr-reveal.js on brand profiles) while any [role=dialog] carries .jm-open. overflow:hidden !important; never set it yourself.

api.name: history
api.desc: Opening pushes a history entry and the device Back button closes the modal, via the same hook. Register a close function in knownCloseFor for modals with teardown.

components.name: Share sheet
components.summary: The portal share sheet as a drop-in: give any element data-share and load /ghar-share.js. The script injects one .jm-modal with a preview card, Copy link, WhatsApp, X, Facebook, LinkedIn and Email tiles, a QR toggle and the native share button, so a page never carries its markup.
use: Sharing the current page or one item on it: a floating Share button on an article, a Share action on a card
An article or episode preview with data-share-variant="story": type-led, eyebrow plus headline, no image and no QR
A template serving many pages from one file: point data-share-title-from and data-share-eyebrow-from at selectors instead of writing the copy
avoid: Brand and person profiles. They carry #brShareModal and data-brand-share (see the profile share sheet); when #brShareModal is on the page this script does nothing
Pasting the sheet's markup or the .bsm-* CSS into a page. The script injects the markup and the styles ship in styles.min.css
An avatar or a person's photo on the story variant. It is type-led by design
Loading a network's share SDK. The tiles are plain links to public share endpoints; the only external call is the QR image, fetched when the reader opens it

Starting an account from a package CTA with openSignUp('superpro'), on a page that carries the full flow

Calling openSignIn on a page without #ocMenu. It reads the off-canvas menu first and throws if it is missing

components.name: Toast
components.summary: A short confirmation or error that appears at the edge of the screen. One function creates the host, stacks them, times them out and animates them away.
use: Confirming something the reader just did: saved, copied, sent
An error that is not tied to one form field
Offering a single Undo right after an action
avoid: Writing .toast markup by hand. The host, stacking and timers only exist in gharToast
An error about one field: use the field error state instead
Anything the reader must read to continue. Errors already persist; a decision needs a dialog

api.name: gharToast(title, opts)
api.desc: Shows a toast. Returns dismiss(), so the caller can close it early.

api.name: opts.type
api.desc: success (default), info, warn or error. Errors are announced assertively.

api.name: opts.body
api.desc: A second line, for detail the title cannot carry.

api.name: opts.duration
api.desc: Milliseconds before it clears. 0 keeps it. Errors default to 0, everything else to 4000.

api.name: opts.action
api.desc: { label, onClick } for one inline action such as Undo.

components.name: Section subnav (L2)
components.summary: The second-level bar of a vertical: icon-over-label tabs with an ink underline on the active one. Its own row on mobile and tablet; from 1080px up it is lifted into the masthead so the page keeps one bar.
use: A vertical hub and its sibling pages where the section tabs are the primary navigation (design, voices, ghartalks)
Any page that wants the masthead to hide on scroll: L1 may only collapse when this bar is there to take the top
avoid: A third bar. A second axis (series, franchise) is an in-page block or the .dp-subnav strip on the page where that axis is the operative one
A tab strip on a results page whose finder already scopes the set (voices-search hides it below 1080)
Toggling body.mainnav-hidden without the gharCanCollapseNav() gate. On desktop the tabs live inside L1 and would leave with it
Hand-setting --subnav-h. syncH() publishes it from the measured height, and 0 is the signal that the bar is merged
Per-page tweaks to a shared vertical's bar (extra active states, hash shims). Sibling pages keep it byte-identical
Using it on /brands, /people or person profiles, whose handoff target is the sticky finder, not an L2 bar

api.name: .subnav-rule

api.name: gharCanCollapseNav()
api.desc: True only when --subnav-h is greater than 0, i.e. a separate L2 bar exists to take the top of the viewport.

api.name: --subnav-h
api.desc: Measured bar height, published by syncH(). Body top padding is --mainnav-h + --subnav-h.

api.name: body.subnav-merged
api.desc: Set when the tabs have moved into the masthead (1080px and up, content-nav pages).

api.name: body.mainnav-hidden

Adding a new overlay panel to the partials without adding its root to the light-token reset in nav.css (or building it on .jm-modal). It renders off-white text on its own white ground

<script type="module">
  import PhotoSwipeLightbox from '/dist/photoswipe/photoswipe-lightbox.esm.min.js';
  const lightbox = new PhotoSwipeLightbox({
    gallery:    '[data-pswp-gallery]',
    children:   'a.pswp-link',
    pswpModule: () => import('/dist/photoswipe/photoswipe.esm.min.js'),
    // `fade` open/close is more forgiving than `zoom` when the thumb
    // crops the image to a different aspect ratio than the hi-res.
    showHideAnimationType: 'fade',
    bgOpacity: 0.95,
    paddingFn: () => ({ top: 30, bottom: 60, left: 0, right: 0 }),
  });
  lightbox.on('uiRegister', function() {
    lightbox.pswp.ui.registerElement({
      name: 'caption',
      order: 9,
      isButton: false,
      appendTo: 'root',
      html: '',
      onInit: (el, pswp) => {
        pswp.on('change', () => {
          const slide = pswp.currSlide;
          const cap = slide?.data?.element?.dataset?.pswpCaption || '';
          el.innerHTML = cap;
        });
      },
    });
  });
  lightbox.init();
</script>
